title: Best Dehumidifier for Bathroom (2026): Portable & Compact Picks
h1: The Best Portable Dehumidifiers for Your Bathroom
dek: A hot shower can push a small bathroom past 90% humidity in minutes. The right dehumidifier clears that spike before mold finds the grout.
description: The best portable dehumidifier for bathroom steam, from compact minis to a 50-pint pick, plus options for small bathrooms and bathrooms without a vent.
intro: A bathroom's humidity problem isn't steady like a basement's; it's a spike. Ten minutes under hot water can drive a small bathroom above **90% relative humidity**, and that moisture settles straight onto grout, caulk, drywall and the ceiling paint. A portable dehumidifier for the bathroom catches that spike and brings the room back down before condensation lingers long enough to feed mold.

Even a working exhaust fan often leaves the job half-done. Many fans are undersized, clogged or switched off the moment the shower ends, and plenty of older bathrooms don't have one at all. A dehumidifier keeps working after the fan stops, which is exactly when mirrors stay fogged and window sills stay wet.
We compared compact and full-size units on extraction speed, noise, footprint and safety near water. Here's what to buy for everything from a busy family bathroom to a powder room.
topPicksLead: The **GE APER50LZ** is our top bathroom pick when you want to clear shower steam fast; for small bathrooms, the compact **Pro Breeze PB-03** fits on a shelf.

products.name: GE 50-Pint Dehumidifier with Built-In Pump (APER50LZ)
pros: 50-pint capacity knocks down a shower spike fast
Built-in pump drains to a sink or tub
cons: Too big for a small or half bath
Needs floor space outside the splash zone
Pump hose needs to stay kink-free
products.whyWeLoveIt: A bathroom's problem is speed: you want the humidity down before the next shower, not eventually. The APER50LZ has the capacity to do that, and its pump means you can run it to the tub or sink drain instead of emptying a bucket.
products.performance: It's a 50-pint compressor unit with an integrated pump, which is plenty for a large primary bath or a bathroom that opens onto a bedroom or laundry area. Set the digital humidistat to around 50% and it works alongside your exhaust fan, shutting off once the room recovers. Owners most often praise the convenience of the pump and flag the usual upkeep: keeping the hose kink-free and the outlet clean. See our [best GE dehumidifier](/best/best-ge-dehumidifier/) guide for the rest of the lineup.

products.name: Frigidaire 22-Pint Dehumidifier (FFAD2233W1)
products.whyWeLoveIt: If 50 pints is more than you need, this 22-pint compressor unit covers a full bathroom for less money and less floor space, with real extraction power that a mini can't match.
products.performance: It removes up to 22 pints a day under the DOE test, enough to handle daily showers in a typical full bath. The easy-clean filter is a smart touch in a room full of towel lint, and the drain port lets it run without nightly bucket checks. Owners describe it as reliable and simple. Compare the range in our [best Frigidaire dehumidifier](/best/best-frigidaire-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.name: Eva-Dry EDV-2400 Dehumidifier with Humidistat
pros: Adjustable humidistat holds a set target
Compact enough for a counter or corner
cons: Far less capacity than the GE or Frigidaire
Pulls less water once the room cools down
products.whyWeLoveIt: It splits the difference between full-size units and the tiniest minis: Eva-Dry's step-up electric model, with more airflow and a bigger tank than its petite sibling, but small enough not to dominate the room. The adjustable humidistat is the key feature, bringing the room down after a shower and then backing off.
products.performance: Rather than running nonstop, it stops at your chosen humidity, which avoids both over-drying and quitting too soon. It's a thermoelectric (Peltier) unit, so there's only a quiet fan running, and like every Peltier design it pulls water most effectively in warm, humid air — which is exactly what a bathroom gives it after a shower. If the room still feels damp with it running, step up to a compressor unit. For more compact choices, browse our [best small dehumidifier](/best/best-small-dehumidifier/) picks.

products.name: Eva-Dry EDV-1100 Petite Dehumidifier
pros: Small enough for a vanity shelf
Auto shut-off when the tank fills
cons: Removes ounces, not pints, per day
Can't keep up with long, hot showers on its own
products.whyWeLoveIt: When a bathroom backs onto a bedroom or nursery, noise matters. The EDV-1100 is quiet enough to fade into the background while it handles everyday humidity between showers.
products.performance: It's a thermoelectric (Peltier) mini rated for about 1,100 cubic feet, so it's near-silent and runs cool on roughly 22 watts. It shuts off when the 16-ounce tank fills and restarts once you empty it. Like all minis, it's best at maintaining a small room rather than rescuing it, so pair it with your exhaust fan during showers. Need quiet elsewhere? See our [best quiet dehumidifier](/best/best-quiet-dehumidifier/) roundup.

products.name: Pro Breeze PB-03 Mini Dehumidifier
pros: Fits on a shelf or toilet-tank lid
Covers up to about 2,200 cubic feet
products.whyWeLoveIt: A half-bath or small bathroom doesn't need big extraction; it needs to stop smelling musty. The PB-03 is the right scale for that job and takes up almost no space.
products.performance: Pro Breeze rates it for spaces up to about 2,200 cubic feet, which covers most small bathrooms and powder rooms. As a thermoelectric unit it's quiet and gentle, so it suits steady, light humidity better than a daily steam cloud. Owners like it for powder rooms, small guest baths and RV bathrooms.

blocks.text: That gap between 90% and 50% is why bathrooms are often the most mold-prone rooms in a house that's otherwise dry. Daily spikes, slow recovery and cool surfaces like tile and window glass give mold everything it needs.

sections.heading: How we pick the best bathroom dehumidifiers

blocks.text: We don't run a test lab. We compared manufacturer capacity and coverage ratings, DOE and ENERGY STAR data where available, noise ratings, and manuals for safety guidance around water. We checked the CPSC database for recalls and read owner reviews from people using these units in bathrooms specifically, looking for issues like corrosion, tank leaks and noise.
Because bathrooms vary so much, we picked across sizes: a high-capacity unit for busy family bathrooms, mid-size options and quiet minis for small or adjoining spaces.

sections.heading: What to look for in a bathroom dehumidifier

items.label: The right size
items.text: Small or half bath: a compact or mini dehumidifier. Full bath with daily showers: 20–22 pints. Large or shared bath: 30–50 pints.

items.label: A humidistat
items.text: Set it to about 50% so the unit shuts off once the room recovers. Our [humidistat settings guide](/guides/dehumidifier-humidistat-settings-guide/) has more targets.

items.label: Electrical safety
items.text: Plug into a GFCI-protected outlet, as required for bathroom circuits, and keep the unit well away from the tub and shower spray.

items.label: Quiet operation
items.text: If the bathroom adjoins a bedroom, prioritize a thermoelectric mini or a unit with a low fan setting.

items.label: Easy draining
items.text: A continuous-drain hose into the tub or shower pan saves daily emptying.

sections.heading: Best dehumidifier for a bathroom without a vent

blocks.text: A bathroom with no exhaust fan has nowhere to send shower steam, so a dehumidifier does all the work. Size up: choose a compressor unit such as the Frigidaire FFAD2233W1 for a small bath or the GE APER50LZ for a larger one, rather than a mini. Run it during and for 30–60 minutes after each shower, and crack the door to let air circulate.

Cordless renewable units, like the silica-based minis in our [Eva-Dry](/best/best-eva-dry-dehumidifier/) guide, are handy for a cabinet or linen closet but can't keep up with shower steam. For a permanent, off-the-floor solution, see our [wall-mounted dehumidifier](/best/best-wall-mounted-dehumidifier/) picks.
Bathroom fan with a dehumidifier sensor

Humidity-sensing exhaust fans switch on automatically when moisture rises and run until it falls. If you're replacing a fan anyway, one is a great upgrade — but it still vents air outdoors rather than drying it, so in a windowless bath a portable dehumidifier remains a helpful partner.

items: Run the exhaust fan during your shower and for at least 20 minutes afterward.
Turn on the dehumidifier set to about 50% and leave it running until it cycles off.
Squeegee glass and tile, and hang towels to dry outside the bathroom if you can.
Leave the door open after showers so drier air from the house can mix in.
Clean grout and caulk regularly, and recaulk anywhere it's cracked or discolored.

blocks.title: Already seeing mold?
blocks.text: A dehumidifier stops new growth but won't remove what's there. Clean it first, then keep humidity down. Our [black mold](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-black-mold/) guide has more.

For a busy or large bathroom, the **GE APER50LZ** clears shower steam fastest. Choose the **Frigidaire FFAD2233W1** for a full small bathroom on a budget, the **Eva-Dry EDV-2400** for a mid-size room with automatic control, the **Eva-Dry EDV-1100** when quiet matters, and the **Pro Breeze PB-03** for a powder room or small bath. Pair any of them with your exhaust fan and a GFCI outlet, and your grout will thank you.

faqs.q: What is the best portable dehumidifier for a bathroom?
faqs.a: For a large or busy bathroom, the GE APER50LZ clears post-shower humidity fastest. For a small bathroom or powder room, the compact Pro Breeze PB-03 fits on a shelf, and the Eva-Dry EDV-1100 is the quietest pick for a bathroom next to a bedroom.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier for a small bathroom?
faqs.a: A compact unit is usually enough. The Pro Breeze PB-03 covers up to about 2,200 cubic feet and is near-silent. If the small bathroom has a daily shower and no fan, step up to a compact compressor model like the Frigidaire FFAD2233W1.

faqs.q: Do I need a dehumidifier if my bathroom has an exhaust fan?
faqs.a: Often yes. Many fans are undersized, clogged or switched off too soon. A dehumidifier handles the moisture a fan leaves behind and keeps working after the fan stops.

faqs.q: Is it safe to use a dehumidifier in a bathroom?
faqs.a: Yes, with precautions. Keep it out of the spray zone, plug it into a GFCI-protected outlet and never handle it with wet hands. Empty or drain the tank so it can't tip and spill.

faqs.q: What's the best dehumidifier for a bathroom without a vent?
faqs.a: Choose a compressor unit rather than a mini, since it has to handle all the steam on its own. A 22-pint model suits a small bath and a 50-pint model a larger one. Run it during and after every shower.

faqs.q: Are there wall-mounted dehumidifiers for bathrooms?
faqs.a: Yes. Wall-mounted units keep the floor clear and away from splashes, and some are designed for bathrooms and pool rooms. See our [wall-mounted dehumidifier](/best/best-wall-mounted-dehumidifier/) guide for options and installation considerations.
